en: Boiling liquid water to 100 degrees Celsius for one minute kills harmful bacteria, making it safe to drink.
Mixing liquid bleach and vinegar creates toxic chlorine gas, so you must never combine these two common cleaning solutions.
Drinking a mixture of water, salt, and sugar replaces lost fluids and electrolytes when you have severe diarrhea.
Applying solid ice directly to a severe burn can damage the skin, so use cool running liquid water instead.
Liquefied petroleum gas expands rapidly into a highly flammable gas when it leaks from a tank, creating a fire hazard.
Puncturing your skin with dirty metal introduces soil bacteria that cause tetanus, requiring a doctor to administer a vaccine.
Fine solid particles of flour suspended in the air can ignite and cause a dust explosion near an open flame.
Touching solid dry ice, which is negative 78 degrees Celsius, causes severe frostbite, so always handle it with thick gloves.
Pouring boiling liquid water into a cold solid glass pitcher causes rapid thermal expansion, making the glass shatter dangerously.
Burning charcoal in a closed room produces odorless carbon monoxide gas, which blocks oxygen in your blood and causes death.
Pouring liquid water onto a burning grease fire causes the water to vaporize instantly, spreading the burning oil everywhere.
Mixing solid baking soda with liquid stomach acid produces carbon dioxide gas, which you burp out to relieve indigestion.
